situation:
You are to assume the role of regional manager at FOXGLOVE BOOKSELLERS, a chain of twenty-two bookstores. The owner (judge) has asked you to recommend what the chain should do about the way it uses what its loyalty program records, after a complaint reached the owner (judge) directly.

New leadership arrived two years ago, following two losing years, and rebuilt the chain around what the loyalty program shows: which titles each member buys, how often, and in which store. Those records now decide staffing hours, shelf space, and which mailers each member receives. The terms members agree to permit all of it.

A loyalty member complained after a mailer arrived recommending titles that followed a private medical purchase made in one store, and asked the owner (judge) to stop the chain from using purchases like that one. Store staff have taken the complaints at the counter, and several have said they are uncomfortable explaining a practice they did not design.

Continuing to target mailers by purchase history leaves store staff facing those customers; narrowing the program to store-level totals costs the chain the detail it now uses to set staffing hours and shelf space. The owner (judge) wants your recommendation and how it would be explained. The owner (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
